question:
In a triangle ABC, if AD is the angle bisector of ∠BAC, AE ⊥ BC, ∠B = 30° and ∠C = 50°, then ∠DAE is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e00fe19c01f5b468e985c46217c4d984e4d5adfae0c3a719407d89cd2587ca7a.png]
solution:
**Given:**

AD is the angle bisector of ∠BAC

AE ⊥ BC

∠B = 30°

∠C = 50°

**Concept used:**

Sum of angles of triangle is 180°

**Calculations:**

As, AE is perpendicular to BE, so we can say that

⇒ ∠AEB = ∠CEA = 90°

In triangleAEB

⇒ ∠EBA + ∠EAB + ∠AEB = 180°

⇒ 30° + ∠EAB + 90° = 180°

⇒ ∠EAB = 180° - 120° = 60°

Now,

In triangleABC

⇒ ∠CBA + ∠CAB + ∠ACB = 180°

⇒ 30° + ∠CAB + 50° = 180°

⇒ ∠CAB = 180° - 80° = 100°

we know that, AD is bisector of ∠CAB

so, Bisector will divide the ∠A into equal parts

⇒ ∠DAB = ∠DAC = 100° / 2 = 50°

⇒ ∠DAE = ∠EAB - ∠DAB = 60° - 50° = 10°

**⇒ Hence, ∠****DAE is equivalent to 10**°
